script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Sports
Theme: ambition

Begin screenplay.

---

FADE IN:

EXT. PARK - DAY

A beautiful, sunlit park, children playing, parents picnicking.

A YOUNG ATHLETE, JASON, practices martial arts moves alone. Passersby look at him curiously, but keep walking.

INT. JASON'S LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Jason sits in front of an old TV, watching a professional basketball game. He dreams of playing on that court one day.

JASON (to himself)
(whispering)
One day...

Suddenly, a knock at the door. It's his neighbor, MIKE, a former professional basketball player.

MIKE
Hey Jason, long time no see. Mind if I come in?

JASON
(surprised)
Oh, hi Mike! Sure, come on in.

INT. JASON'S LIVING ROOM - LATER

Mike sits next to Jason and they watch the game together.

MIKE
You know, I used to play professionally back in the day.

JASON
(wide-eyed)
Really? That's amazing! What position did you play?

MIKE
Power forward. And I want you to know something, Jason. You've got what it takes to make it to the big leagues.

JASON
(excited)
Really? You think so?

MIKE
Absolutely. But you'll need more than just skill. You'll need dedication, ambition, and a little bit of luck.

INT. JASON'S BEDROOM - NIGHT

Jason sits at his desk, staring at a basketball hoop poster on the wall. He makes a decision.

JASON
(to himself)
I'll make it to the big leagues, no matter what it takes.

EXT. SCHOOL - DAY

Jason runs through the halls, late for class. He arrives, out of breath, just in time.

MS. JONES
(stern)
Jason, you're always late. If you can't manage your time, you won't make it far in life.

JASON
(determined)
I'll manage, Ms. Jones. I promise.

INT. GYM - NIGHT

Jason works out, pushing himself to the limit. He's sweaty, exhausted, but determined.

Suddenly, the GYM COACH enters.

COACH
(surprised)
Jason, what are you doing here so late?

JASON
(panting)
I wanted to practice some more. I'm determined to make the varsity team.

COACH
(impressed)
I like your attitude, son. You've got what it takes.

INT. BASKETBALL COURT - DAY

Jason plays a pickup game with some older, experienced players. They mock him at first, but he proves himself worthy.

LATER, as they leave the court, one of the players, OLD TRASH TALKER, sneers at Jason.

OLD TRASH TALKER
(mocking)
You think you're something special, kid? You'll never make it.

JASON
(calmly)
We'll see about that.

EXT. PARK - NIGHT

Jason practices his moves alone, as he has done for months. He's gotten stronger, faster, better.

Suddenly, Mike appears.

MIKE
(proud)
Look at you, Jason. You've come a long way.

JASON
(determined)
I'm not done yet, Mike. I'll make it to the big leagues.

MIKE
(smiling)
I believe in you, son. Keep pushing yourself.

INT. BASKETBALL COURT - DAY

Jason plays in a scouting tournament. He's nervous, but focused. He plays well, impressing the scouts.

LATER, as he packs up his things, a SCOUT approaches him.

SCOUT
Jason, we've seen potential in you. We'd like to offer you a spot on our development team.

JASON
(overjoyed)
Thank you, sir! I won't let you down.

INT. JASON'S LIVING ROOM - NIGHT

Jason sits in front of the TV, watching himself play in a professional game. He's made it.

JASON
(whispering)
I made it...

FADE OUT.

---

End of screenplay.
